stories.headline: Bones recovered from Philadelphia backyard dig at home tied to seven missing women
stories.summary: Sources tell Action News the Philadelphia Medical Examiner’s Office was called Thursday to recover bones from the backyard of 417 W. Chew Ave. in Olney — the former home of late violent pornographer Raymond “R.C.” Horsch and his son Eugene — and that the remains’ condition and origin are not yet known. The bones will go to a lab to determine whether they are human and whether they connect to an investigation that has linked seven missing women to the property through videos and images, though no bodies have been found. Crews began excavating Tuesday after luminol testing earlier in the week produced a positive reaction that may indicate DNA evidence; a safe was also found behind a wall. Eugene Horsch was arrested in June on federal firearms and drug charges that led investigators to the house; he has not been charged in the missing-women probe.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo pre-orders already show January 2027 shipping — sold out for Christmas
stories.summary: Hours after pre-orders opened Friday morning, Apple’s U.S. online store was quoting an estimated ship date of January 25, 2027 for every iPhone Duo configuration — past Christmas and the furthest slip MacRumors has seen on a new iPhone. Store pickup reservation slots for the Oct. 23 launch day were already gone, with Apple telling shoppers to check back Saturday, Oct. 24. Walk-in inventory on launch day is expected to be tight. The $1,999 foldable has faced production constraints; a supply-chain source told China’s Jiemian News that Foxconn final-assembly yields were only slightly above 60% as of mid-September under Apple’s quality standards. You can still place an order; you just will not get one with the first wave.

stories.headline: Twin Brooks Park playground closed for maintenance and deep cleaning
stories.summary: Trumbull Parks & Recreation says the playground at Twin Brooks Park is closed for routine maintenance, minor repairs, and a thorough deep cleaning so it is safe and ready to reopen. The town expects the work to finish and the playground to reopen in just a few days, and asks residents not to take down the caution tape. The CivicAlert (AID 3200) was posted Friday, Oct. 16.

stories.headline: Iron Maiden adds a surprise final 2027 North American leg of Run For Your Lives
stories.summary: Live Nation announced that Iron Maiden will return to North America in spring 2027 for a third and final leg of its 50th-anniversary Run For Your Lives tour — 16 more dates after the band had planned a live break that year. Bassist Steve Harris said the just-finished U.S./Canada run went so well the band decided to hit regions it missed, especially the Northwest and Southeast, and to close with festival headlines at Sonic Temple in Columbus and Boardwalk Rock in Maryland. The bill is all-British: Bullet For My Valentine and The Raven Age open. Dates include Tacoma, Vancouver, Portland, Hartford’s Meadows (May 9), and UBS Arena; artist presale starts Monday, Oct. 19, with general onsale Friday, Oct. 23. By the end the tour will have played 107 shows in 36 countries.

stories.headline: Penguins visit Avalanche tonight as Crosby and MacKinnon meet for the 21st time
stories.summary: Pittsburgh (3-3-1) continues its four-game road trip at Colorado (4-2-1) tonight at Ball Arena, 9 p.m. ET on SportsNet Pittsburgh. Cole Harbour buddies Sidney Crosby and Nathan MacKinnon face each other for the first time this season and the 21st time in their NHL careers; MacKinnon holds a 26–17 points edge and an 11-6-3 record in their prior meetings, while Crosby has points in six of his last seven vs. the Avalanche. Crosby scored his first two goals of the season in Tuesday’s 5-3 loss at Chicago; MacKinnon leads Colorado with 12 points in seven games. Bryan Rust rides a nine-game point streak against the Avs, and Evgeni Malkin has 27 points in 25 career games vs. Colorado. Projected Pens lines still feature Rakell-Crosby-Rust and Chinakhov-Novak-Malkin.

stories.headline: U.S. Treasurer challenges Americans to spend Trump $1 coins at “liberal coffee shops”
stories.summary: In a Treasury Department TikTok, U.S. Treasurer Brandon Beach held up the new Donald Trump dollar coin — part of the nation’s 250th-anniversary commemoratives — and challenged viewers to get a roll at banks next month, then buy coffee “at your favorite liberal coffee shop” and “watch their heads explode.” The U.S. Mint has sold the coins since September (a roll of 25 for $61 and a bag of 100 for $154.50, above face value) and says they are legal tender; Beach’s pitch suggests bank distribution at face value may follow. The coin shows Trump under “LIBERTY” with “1776 ~ 2026.” Fox Business said Treasury had not yet clarified which banks will stock them or at what price.

stories.headline: Analogue refreshes Super Nt and Mega Sg with USB-C, wireless controllers, hot-swap carts
stories.summary: Analogue announced Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus — FPGA recreations of the SNES and Sega Genesis that still play original cartridges, now with a reworked design, USB-C power, a USB-A accessory port, and built-in Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz wireless for controllers (no dongle). Wired pads still work, either console can wake from the primary gamepad, and cartridges can be hot-swapped after quitting through a menu. Output remains 1080p (not 4K like Analogue 3D). Preorders open Monday, Oct. 19 at 9 a.m. PT / noon ET for $219.99, with shipping expected in December.

stories.headline: Bend school shooter was stopped by a community member who chased him into the building, police say
stories.summary: Police now say the 16-year-old who shot his way through the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon was shot and killed by a community member who saw him go in, “pursued him into the school and engaged him.” Officers arrived about three minutes after the first 911 call — a driver reporting being shot at by someone with a long gun — and found the suspect already dead. Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher were killed; a 7-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher are in critical condition. Gov. Tina Kotek praised the unnamed bystander who “heroically intervened to stop further loss of life.” Investigators haven’t said how the teen got the gun — the ATF has run an urgent trace — or whether he had ties to the school. All Bend-La Pine schools are closed Friday.

stories.headline: White House declassifies documents it says undercut key claims behind Trump’s 2019 impeachment
stories.summary: The White House released declassified records late Thursday that it says cast doubt on the case House Democrats built for Trump’s first impeachment. An administration official said the papers show Joe Biden’s career staff supported both the $1 billion Ukraine loan guarantee and Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin — who was investigating Burisma — before Biden demanded Shokin’s firing as a condition of the loan. A November 2016 email from diplomat George Kent warned that Hunter Biden’s seat on the Burisma board “undercut the anti-corruption message” the U.S. was pushing in Ukraine, and other emails show Ambassador Marie Yovanovitch, a key impeachment witness, was briefed on Burisma and the Bidens. The official also said the whistleblower who triggered the probe had no firsthand knowledge of Trump’s 2019 call with Zelensky. Trump was impeached in 2019 and acquitted by the Senate in 2020.

stories.headline: Apple Store goes dark as $1,999 iPhone Duo pre-orders open at 8 a.m. ET today
stories.summary: Apple’s online store went down early Friday ahead of pre-orders for the iPhone Duo, its first foldable, with a placeholder reading “We love that early energy. … Pre-order begins at 5:00 a.m. PT.” Orders open at 8 a.m. Eastern in more than 70 countries, and with demand expected to be high and supply tight, pre-ordering is likely the best bet; deliveries and in-store sales start Friday, Oct. 23. The Duo starts at $1,999 in Star White or Night Sky, with 256GB up to 2TB of storage. It pairs a 5.4-inch outer screen with a 7.6-inch, nearly creaseless inner OLED that unfolds into a small iPad. Engadget, which called it “Apple’s most exciting device in a decade,” notes the trade-offs: no Face ID, no variable-aperture main camera like the iPhone 18 Pro, and a weaker under-display selfie camera on the inner screen.

stories.headline: Brewers sweep the two-time champion Dodgers to reach their first World Series since 1982
stories.summary: Milwaukee finished a four-game NLCS sweep of Los Angeles with a 6–4 comeback win Thursday night, ending the Dodgers’ bid to become just the third franchise, after the Yankees and A’s, to win three straight titles. The Dodgers led 4–0 in the second inning after an Andy Pages RBI single and a 428-foot, three-run homer from Shohei Ohtani. Jake Bauers’ two-run double and a David Hamilton RBI single chipped away, a bases-loaded walk tied it, Garrett Mitchell’s solo shot in the sixth put the Brewers ahead, and Hamilton homered in the ninth. “It’s absolutely surreal,” Mitchell said. Milwaukee, which has never won a World Series, will face the winner of Cleveland vs. Tampa Bay.

stories.headline: Reported ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz hit a record 12 in one week
stories.summary: Twelve vessels reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz from Oct. 5 to 11, the most in any week since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, according to a BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data. Six were hit on Sunday alone, and four more attacks have been reported this week, including the container ship GFS Pride, which sank Tuesday after its 21 crew were evacuated. Experts say Tehran is striking ships to reassert control of the waterway as U.S. forces escort more tankers through the strait, and it is hitting targets farther afield, such as a tanker set ablaze off Oman more than 150 miles away and another struck north of Qatar. Central Command says escorted commercial traffic is still moving, but the September rebound in Gulf oil shipments has slowed.

stories.headline: Trivium’s Matt Heafy says he walked out and quit the band last year — until his wife talked him back
stories.summary: Trivium frontman Matt Heafy told Metal Hammer that in mid-2025, right after the band’s 20th-anniversary Ascendancy tour, the band’s chemistry was “falling apart” and he hit his breaking point while tracking guitars at their rehearsal hangar. “I stand up. I leave. I call [my wife] Ashley. I’m like, ‘I’m done with this band. I can’t do this anymore,’” he said, describing driving home and switching off his phone. Ashley let the dust settle and told him he couldn’t quit, so he went back. The problems continued, though, and drummer Alex Bent left that October. Heafy won’t air the “dirty laundry,” but he says the change saved the band: without it Trivium “would have been done,” and now “we are tighter live than we’ve ever been.”

stories.headline: License-plate camera helps Wisconsin police nab Iowa man suspected of stealing $18,000 in LEGO from Walmarts
stories.summary: Sun Prairie, Wisconsin, police arrested 28-year-old Willie Dean of Iowa City on Wednesday after a Walmart called in an active retail theft. Officers were already nearby because an automatic license-plate reader had flagged a vehicle tied to earlier thefts. Dean ran from the store, but officers caught him in a nearby backyard, where police say he resisted before being taken into custody. Investigators believe he is behind thefts of more than $18,000 worth of LEGO from Walmart stores across Wisconsin and Illinois; about $1,500 worth was recovered. He also had a nationwide extraditable warrant on burglary and theft counts. He was booked on retail theft, resisting an officer, and misdemeanor and felony bail-jumping charges as other agencies work out how far the thefts reach.

stories.headline: Tesla finally reveals the next-gen Roadster — it drove upside down, flew, flipped and landed
stories.summary: Nearly nine years after the first tease, Tesla showed the new Roadster Thursday night at an event near SpaceX’s McGregor site outside Waco, Texas. Using fans and cold-gas thrusters, the car drove up a curved ramp until it was upside down, flew off, flipped and landed, then hovered over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Semi, Model Y and Model 3. “Well, it worked,” Elon Musk said. “Flying cars are real.” Tesla lists three versions: a two-seat road-ready Performance model (0–60 in under 1.6 seconds), a two-seat race-ready Thrust model with rear thrusters (under 0.9 seconds), and an invite-only single-seat Rocket (under 0.59 seconds, 230+ mph top speed, 300+ miles of range). Pricing wasn’t given; reservations reopened in the configurator, and production is planned for Giga Texas in 2027 or 2028.

stories.headline: Trump calls Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed “100% Muslim Brotherhood” and a “con man”
stories.summary: At a White House Rose Garden lunch Thursday, President Trump went after Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee: “He’s a Muslim Brotherhood guy, 100%. … How about having him be on the Senate Intelligence Committee?” Trump also called him a “fraud” and “con man” and said he would visit Michigan to “expose” him. The attacks follow fresh scrutiny of 2012 posts by El-Sayed’s half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, saying their mother was active in the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt in the early 1970s and that “my family has long been MB.” El-Sayed denies any family ties and says his opponent, Republican Mike Rogers, is attacking his name and faith instead of his policies. The clash comes after a tense NBC interview in which he was pressed on the posts.

stories.headline: Body found in a barrel at Lake Mead in 2022 identified as 1980s murder victim; killer still unknown
stories.summary: Four years after the bones of a man shot in the head were found in a deteriorated 50-gallon drum as Lake Mead’s waters receded, Clark County Coroner Melanie Rouse on Thursday identified him as Edward Lelburian Jackson, a man in his mid-to-late 50s from Arkansas. Las Vegas police believe he was killed in the early 1980s, based on clothing remnants and family interviews, but don’t know who did it. Despite years of speculation about the mob, homicide Lt. Robert Price said investigators have nothing to support organized-crime theories; Jackson traveled the country, had no known Las Vegas ties or gambling history, and had a Utah record for aggravated arson and fraud conspiracy. Genealogical DNA testing by Oklahoma State University cracked the ID.

stories.headline: KK’s Priest re-records Judas Priest’s “Never Satisfied” with Ripper Owens — and fans slam the AI video
stories.summary: Former Judas Priest guitarist KK Downing’s band KK’s Priest has released a new version of Priest’s 1974 classic “Never Satisfied,” sung by ex-Priest frontman Tim “Ripper” Owens. The video uses AI to recreate a young Downing staring into a guitar-shop window and stepping off a bus with his case before heading for stardom — and many fans aren’t buying it (“Love the song, but goddam I hate the AI slop”). Downing defended it as something “absolutely impossible to create or film today” without the technology, and said of Owens versus Rob Halford on the original: “Two great singers and performers.” Producer JPSR Studio openly bills itself as an AI-native production house.

stories.headline: Drone strikes on tankers in Romanian waters raise fears Russia’s war is spilling into NATO territory
stories.summary: Romania launched search-and-rescue operations off its Black Sea coast Thursday after a drone hit the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader about 15 miles southeast of the port of Sulina, setting it ablaze; five crew were rescued and seven are missing. President Nicusor Dan said another ship, the Comoros-flagged Yara J, was struck the night before in Romanian territorial waters, though he didn’t say where the drones came from. Romania’s defense ministry tracked a “group of air targets” near Ukraine’s Snake Island overnight and a drone briefly entered Romanian airspace. It follows Tuesday’s drone strikes on two ships off Bulgaria that left 11 crew missing — a spate of attacks inside the waters of NATO and EU members.

stories.headline: Yashica’s tiny 1959-style Y16 pocket camera gets a $119 price and late-November ship date
stories.summary: Yashica has fully announced the Y16, a pocket digital camera styled after the original company’s 1959 Y16. It pairs a 12MP sensor with a 27mm-equivalent F12 lens, an optical viewfinder, a 1.45-inch screen and a real xenon flash good to about 6.5 feet, plus a top dial with built-in filter looks. At 93 grams (3.3 oz) and 3.6 × 1.8 × 1.1 inches it fits in any pocket, and it ships with an 8GB microSD card. DPReview warns image quality will trail a typical smartphone — the lo-fi look is the point. Price is $119, pre-orders are open, and shipping is expected in late November. Today’s Yashica brand is licensed from Kyocera to Hong Kong-based 100 Enterprises.
